title: Revocation after delegation, before effect
proposed_by: Ben Le, extending Alexander's mid-transaction case and Iman Schrock's before-effect run
drafts: draft-le-agent-passport Sections 'Chain Validation', 'Status and Revocation', 'Exposure After Revocation'
setup: Agent A (domain A) holds a root receipt and delegates to agent B with a child receipt.
B's call to the enforcing service E (domain B) succeeds once. E's protected operation is high value.
Status-list TTL at E: 60 s. B's passport and receipt are not revoked and not expired.

cases.name: revoke-upstream
cases.do: Revoke A's passport. B calls E again (same chain).
cases.note: Revoking a passport invalidates every chain in which its holder delegated.

cases.name: before-effect
cases.do: Revoke A after E has authorized B's request but before the operation takes effect; E revalidates before effect.
cases.note: Iman's expected result: once the enforcing service sees the revocation, the protected operation produces no effect.

measure.t_first_refusal_s: time from the revocation being recorded at the issuer to E's first refusal
measure.t_last_acceptance_s: time from the revocation to E's last acceptance
measure.bound_s: min(remaining passport lifetime, status-list ttl + grace, controller cache bound, issuer-key refresh bound); -01 'Exposure After Revocation'

implementations_offered: MintID (Marc Miro): ZKP non-revocation against a status commitment the issuer publishes every 30 s, verifier accepts at most 180 s; fresh audience-bound proof, lifetime 10 s, before effect. Revocation bounds: issuer revocation 185 s; holder self-revocation 245 s. One run on 13 Nov (1 min 45 s, setup and both paths included): issuer revocation — last acceptance 19.7 s, first refusal 25.2 s; holder self-revocation — last acceptance 14.6 s, first refusal 17.1 s. The 13 Nov figures are measurements from one run; only the bounds are promised. Refusals carry one shared code; the witness-refresh control supplies the revocation attribution (the issuer refuses the revoked credential's witness refresh, while a never-revoked credential refreshes and is accepted again).

reasons.status-revoked: the status list says revoked (confirmed revocation)
reasons.status-stale: the RP's cached list is past its ttl and a fresh one could not be fetched
reasons.status-unavailable: no valid list and no cached copy (service down, invalid list)
reasons.status-grace: allowed under a bounded low-value grace period (log on every use)

reason_mapping: Implementations keep their own codes; state the mapping to these names once per implementation in the run notes. The point is that the three status refusals stay distinguishable in the log even when policy denies all three.
